correctness.rationale: The claim uses all sufficiently large denominators q, every numerator prime to q, v strictly below q, and fixed cutoff L. If r=0, restrict to positive multiples of M=m ceil(L/m) and apply pigeonhole to floor((q-1)/M)+1 circle points to get error at most M/q. For odd v an inverse or its negative has an odd representative; if it is below L, an odd multiplier bounded by L+2 reaches L without reaching q for sufficiently large q. These give exponent 1, which is maximal since every nonzero modular distance is at least 1/q. For m>=3, take p=t, q=mt-1 for r=1 and q=mt+1 for r>=2. The fractional part for every admissible v lies respectively in (1/m,2/m) or ((r-1)/m,r/m), both contained in [1/m,1-1/m]. The pairs are reduced and unbounded in q, ruling out every positive exponent; zero is admissible once the progression is nonempty below q. The two mod-4 classes partition the odd class, as claimed.
residual_risks: Finite replay is diagnostic; the uniform arithmetic argument proves the quantifiers.
